requirements.title: Asynchronous reset and invalidation scan
requirements.definition: rst_i is an active-high asynchronous reset; control enters the invalidation scan 1ns after assertion: stall_request=1, restart_request=0, refill_request=0, refilling=0, and refill_address is unknown. After deassertion, all tags are invalidated one cycle at a time from set=sets-1 down to 0, entering the query-ready phase after exactly sets rising edges.
requirements.timing: All registered control outputs update 1ns after an active rising edge or reset event; RAM updates only on rising edges. The scan cursor is continuously reloaded during reset.
requirements.boundary: Neither reset nor dflush clears the data RAM; previously written contents are retained. No definite numerical value is guaranteed for initially uninitialized data.

requirements.title: Read address and data
requirements.definition: A rising edge with stall_x=0 latches the word index and set index of address_x; after 1ns, load_data continuously reflects the selected stored word. With stall_x=1, the previous read index is retained.
requirements.timing: load_data is not masked by load_q_m or a tag hit; no output is guaranteed before the first reset.
requirements.boundary: The lowest 2 bits of the 32-bit address do not participate in the word index, and the highest 4 bits do not participate in the tag; see the two profiles in the port documentation.

requirements.title: Hits and misses
requirements.definition: In the query-ready phase, the valid tag of the latched read set is compared with the current address_m[27:tag_lsb]. When load_q_m=1 and stall_m=0 and there is no hit, refill is entered after the edge, refill_request=1, and the full 32-bit address_m is saved to refill_address.
requirements.timing: Miss detection uses the inputs stable before the edge and the latched tag; address_x usually leads by one cycle, and the two addresses are allowed to differ, with behavior defined by this clause.
requirements.boundary: load_q_m=0, stall_m=1, or a hit does not initiate a miss; a miss takes priority over dflush on the same edge.

requirements.title: Four-word refill
requirements.definition: During the refill phase, 4 32-bit refill_data words are accepted in sequence on rising edges with refill_ready=1 and written to word0, 1, 2, 3 of the line containing the saved address; the starting point is independent of the input address's word offset; ready=0 does not advance progress. When the last word is written, the tag is marked valid and the query-ready phase is reentered.
requirements.timing: refill_request is 1 only for the cycle after entering refill and is deasserted on the first rising edge of refill; refill_address is retained until the next miss or reset.
requirements.boundary: A legal environment provides refill_ready only within the refill window and deasserts it after the fourth word; the tag of an incomplete refill is invalid.

requirements.title: Stall and restart
requirements.definition: stall_request is 1 during the invalidation scan or refill phase and 0 during the query-ready phase. After each rising edge, refilling reflects whether the phase before the edge was refill, lagging phase transitions by one cycle. restart_request is set to 1 when the last word is accepted; it is cleared on a rising edge in the query-ready phase with stall_a=0, and otherwise retained.
requirements.timing: The final refill on the same edge takes priority in setting restart; clearing according to stall_a occurs only on the next query-ready edge.
requirements.boundary: Progress is retained through arbitrary gaps while waiting for refill_ready, and stall_a can extend restart.

requirements.title: Store hits and byte selection
requirements.definition: In the query-ready phase, when store_q_m=1 and the tag of the latched read set hits the current address_m and stall_m=0, the word corresponding to address_m is written. Bit j of store_byte_select selects store_data[8*j+:8]. No write occurs on a miss or with stall_m=1.
requirements.timing: Writes take effect 1ns after the rising edge; load_q_m and store_q_m can be independent.
requirements.boundary: In the 512-set configuration, unselected bytes retain the original values of the target write word; in the 64-set configuration, unselected bytes are taken from load_data before the edge, so unselected bytes can differ when the two addresses select different words.

requirements.title: Software flush and priority
requirements.definition: When query-ready and there is no acceptable load miss, dflush=1 makes the next phase the invalidation scan, which then invalidates all tags in sequence over sets rising edges. dflush and load requests are ignored during the scan.
requirements.timing: The scan cursor decrements from sets-1 to 0 and wraps around; completion of the scan returns to query-ready.
requirements.boundary: When a miss and dflush both occur on the same edge, the miss is handled first; dflush is not queued during refill. Data is not zeroed.

requirements.title: Indexing and conflict replacement
requirements.definition: Fixed single-way direct mapping: a line is 16 bytes; for 512 sets, set=address[12:4], word=address[12:2], tag=address[27:13]; for 64 sets, set=address[9:4], word=address[9:2], tag=address[27:10]. When different tags map to the same set, a new refill replaces the old tag and all 4 words.
requirements.timing: The read index comes from the latched address_x; the write word index comes from address_m or the refill sequence.
requirements.boundary: The native parameters base_address and limit do not determine the range in the fixed implementation; the fixed macros CFG_DCACHE_BASE_ADDRESS=0, CFG_DCACHE_LIMIT=0x0fffffff determine that the highest tag bit is 27. associativity=1, bytes_per_line=16.
